sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Anti-FLAG immunofluorescence confirmed surface expression of the FLAG-tagged NMBR construct; receptor signalling function was not explicitly assayed in the cited experiment.
sites.rationale: NMBR has no native signal peptide (raw topology begins O at residue 1); the exogenous signal sequence in the TANGO construct is added solely to drive membrane insertion. After signal cleavage, the FLAG tag is left at the extracellular N-terminus immediately before canonical residue 1 (M), making insert_after_residue=0 the only possible junction. No specific residue number is stated in either L1 or L2, so the position is topology-derived: the N-terminus (residues 1–44) is the sole extracellular terminus of this 7-TM receptor, and the C-terminus (residues 328–390) is intracellular. Python confirmed residue 1 = M and residue 45 = V (first TM boundary), placing the tag well outside the TM core. Full-length NMBR was expressed in the TANGO assay platform with an exogenous cleavable signal sequence prepended to a FLAG epitope tag at the N-terminus of the receptor. The construct was transfected into cells and examined by anti-FLAG immunofluorescence for both total and surface expression, confirming cell-surface display.

sources.claim: At the 5′-end, we included a cleavable signal sequence to promote membrane localization 23 and a FLAG epitope tag in order to be able to monitor cell surface expression by immunohistochemistry.

literature_notes: L1 and L2 describe the same TANGO-assay construct and ground a single site. No residue number is named in either clip, so the position is topology-derived from the sole extracellular terminus. The intracellular C-terminus (residues 328–390) is not a surface site. ECL1 (102–118), ECL2 (182–210), and ECL3 (288–303) have no ledger support whatsoever and were not proposed.
